products.name: Puffed Rice
products.shortDescription: Light, airy and crunchy — naturally puffed long-grain brown rice with just a pinch of salt.
products.description:
Just two ingredients: natural long-grain brown rice and salt. Puffed to a perfect crunch and ready for jhal muri, chaat or straight from the bag.

A staple of Bangladeshi tea time, Antar Puffed Rice is naturally puffed — never fried — so it stays light while keeping the toasty flavour of the grain.

preparation.steps: Enjoy straight from the bag, or toss with chopped onion, chilli, mustard oil and lemon for classic jhal muri.
If it has softened after opening, dry-roast in a pan over low heat, stirring constantly, to bring back the crunch.

benefits: Only two ingredients: brown rice and salt
products.storage: Store in a cool, dry place. Reseal after opening.

recipes.title: Classic Jhal Muri
recipes.summary: Kolkata and Dhaka's favourite street snack — spicy, tangy and ready in minutes.
ingredients: Chaat masala and salt to taste
steps: Add the puffed rice to a large bowl.
Add onion, chilli, tomato, peanuts and coriander.
Drizzle over the mustard oil and lemon juice, then sprinkle with chaat masala and salt.
Toss quickly and serve straight away while it's crunchy.

recipes.title: Muri Moa (Puffed Rice & Gur Balls)
recipes.summary: A Bengali winter sweet — crunchy puffed rice bound with melted date-palm jaggery.
ingredients: 200g Antar Premium Khejur Patali Gur, chopped
1 tsp ghee or oil for your hands
steps: Melt the gur with the water in a wide pan over low heat until it bubbles and thickens slightly.
Take off the heat, add the puffed rice and stir quickly until every grain is coated.
Grease your hands and press small handfuls into firm balls while the mixture is still warm.
Leave to cool and set, then store in an airtight jar.

recipes.title: Puffed Rice Chaat
recipes.summary: A sweet, tangy, crunchy chaat with yogurt and chutneys.
ingredients: Chaat masala and roasted cumin powder
steps: Mix the puffed rice, potato and onion in a bowl.
Spoon over the yogurt and both chutneys.
Finish with chaat masala, cumin and coriander.
Serve immediately before the puffed rice softens.

hacks.title: Mix just before serving
hacks.body: Puffed rice soaks up moisture fast. Add wet ingredients like lemon, tomato or chutney at the very last moment to keep every bite crunchy.

hacks.title: Crisp it up again
hacks.body: If an open bag has gone soft, a minute or two in a dry pan over low heat (or 3 minutes in a 150°C oven) brings the crunch right back.

hacks.title: Keep it airtight
hacks.body: Once opened, tip the rest into an airtight jar or clip the bag tightly and keep it away from the stove and kettle steam.

faqs.question: Is Antar Puffed Rice fried?
faqs.answer: No. It is naturally puffed from long-grain brown rice, with only a pinch of salt added.

faqs.question: What is the difference between muri and ポン菓子?
faqs.answer: Both are puffed rice. Bangladeshi muri is lightly salted and used in savoury snacks like jhal muri, while Japanese ポン菓子 is usually sweetened. Antar Puffed Rice is the classic salted muri.

faqs.question: How long does it stay fresh after opening?
faqs.answer: Kept airtight in a cool, dry place it stays crunchy for about two weeks.

faqs.question: Is it halal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every Antar product is halal certified and made without harmful preservatives.

products.name: Punjabi Aloo Samosa
products.nameJp: パンジャビアルーサモサ
products.shortDescription: Flaky golden pastry packed with spiced potato and a fiery chilli kick.
products.description:
Flaky golden pastry packed with spiced potato and a fiery chilli kick. A Punjabi-style samosa made for those who like their snacks hot.

Each box holds 10 generous samosas, ready to fry straight from the freezer — perfect for iftar, parties or an evening snack with chai.

preparation.steps: Do not thaw. Heat oil to 170–175°C and fry from frozen, turning once, until deep golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper.
Preheat the air fryer to 180°C. Lightly brush or spray with oil, cook in a single layer and turn halfway through.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Place on a lined tray, brush lightly with oil and bake, turning halfway, until golden.

benefits: Bold Punjabi-style spice with a chilli kick
Cook straight from frozen — no thawing

recipes.title: Samosa Chaat
recipes.summary: Crushed samosas loaded with chickpeas, yogurt and chutneys — a street-food favourite.
ingredients: Chaat masala, red chilli powder and coriander
steps: Fry or air-fry the samosas until crisp.
Break them roughly onto a plate and top with the warm chickpeas.
Spoon over yogurt, then drizzle both chutneys.
Finish with onion, chaat masala, chilli powder and coriander. Serve straight away.

recipes.title: Samosa Pav
recipes.summary: Mumbai-style samosa sandwich in a soft bun with spicy chutney.
steps: Cook the samosas until golden.
Slice the buns, spread one side with green chutney and the other with tamarind chutney.
Press a hot samosa inside, add onion and close.
Serve warm with a cup of tea.

hacks.title: Never thaw before frying
hacks.body: Frying from frozen keeps the pastry flaky and stops the filling leaking. Thawed samosas soak up oil and go soggy.

hacks.title: Don't crowd the pan
hacks.body: Fry 4–5 at a time so the oil stays hot. Too many at once drops the temperature and makes them greasy.

hacks.title: Too spicy? Add yogurt
hacks.body: Serve with a bowl of cool yogurt raita or a sweet tamarind chutney to balance the chilli heat.

faqs.question: How spicy is the Punjabi Aloo Samosa?
faqs.answer: It is our hottest samosa, with a noticeable green-chilli kick. For a milder taste, try the Antar Vegetable Samosa.

faqs.question: Can I cook it without deep-frying?
faqs.answer: Yes. It crisps up well in an air fryer at 180°C for 12–14 minutes or in the oven at 200°C for 18–20 minutes with a light brush of oil.

faqs.question: Is it vegetarian?
faqs.answer: Yes. The filling is potato, onion and spices, with no meat.

faqs.question: Is it halal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every Antar product is halal certified and made without harmful preservatives.

Preheat the air fryer to 180°C. Lightly brush or spray with oil, cook in a single layer and turn halfway through.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Place on a lined tray, brush lightly with oil and bake, turning halfway, until golden.

benefits: Mild spice the whole family enjoys
Cook straight from frozen — no thawing

recipes.title: Samosa with Mint-Coriander Chutney
recipes.summary: The classic pairing — crisp samosas with a fresh, zingy green chutney.
steps: Blend the coriander, mint, chilli, lemon juice, cumin and salt with a little water until smooth.
Fry, air-fry or bake the samosas until golden.
Serve hot with the chutney for dipping.

recipes.title: Lunchbox Samosa Wrap
recipes.summary: A quick wrap for school or work lunches.
ingredients: 2 tbsp yogurt mixed with a pinch of salt and cumin
steps: Cook the samosas and the flatbreads.
Spread the yogurt sauce over each flatbread.
Add lettuce, cucumber, tomato and two lightly crushed samosas.
Roll up tightly and cut in half.

hacks.title: Reheat in the air fryer
hacks.body: Leftover cooked samosas come back crisp in 3–4 minutes at 180°C in the air fryer. The microwave makes the pastry soft.

hacks.title: Party prep
hacks.body: Fry a batch ahead, then keep them warm and crisp on a rack in a 100°C oven for up to 30 minutes.

faqs.question: Is the Vegetable Samosa spicy?
faqs.answer: No, it is gently spiced and mild enough for children. If you like heat, try the Punjabi Aloo Samosa.

faqs.question: Is it vegetarian?
faqs.answer: Yes. The filling is made with vegetables and spices only.

faqs.question: Do I need to thaw it?
faqs.answer: No. Cook it straight from frozen for the crispiest result.

faqs.question: Is it halal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every Antar product is halal certified and made without harmful preservatives.

products.name: Vegetable Singara
products.shortDescription: Bengal's favourite tea-time bite — a hand-folded, crunchy shell with a hearty veg filling.

Singara has a thicker, crunchier crust than a samosa and a soft, spiced potato filling. Fry it from frozen and serve with hot tea.

Preheat the air fryer to 180°C. Lightly brush or spray with oil, cook in a single layer and turn halfway through.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Place on a lined tray, brush lightly with oil and bake, turning halfway, until golden.

benefits: Cook straight from frozen — no thawing

recipes.title: Singara with Tamarind Chutney
recipes.summary: The tea-stall classic: hot singara with a sweet and sour tamarind dip.
ingredients: 3 tbsp Antar Khejur Patali Gur or brown sugar
Pinch of red chilli powder and salt
steps: Simmer the tamarind, gur and water for 5–6 minutes until glossy and slightly thick.
Stir in the cumin, chilli and salt, then let it cool.
Fry the singaras from frozen until deep golden.
Serve hot with the chutney and a cup of milk tea.

recipes.title: Singara Chaat
recipes.summary: Crushed singara topped with chickpeas, onion and tangy chutney.
steps: Cook the singaras until crisp and break them into pieces on a plate.
Top with chickpeas, onion and chilli.
Drizzle with tamarind chutney and sprinkle with chaat masala and coriander.

hacks.title: Low and slow for the crunch
hacks.body: Singara has a thicker crust than samosa. Fry at a slightly lower heat (around 165–170°C) so the shell cooks through and turns extra crunchy.

hacks.title: The perfect pairing
hacks.body: In Bangladesh singara is eaten with strong milk tea. A hot cup of chai makes it taste just like the tea stall.

faqs.question: What is the difference between singara and samosa?
faqs.answer: Singara is the Bengali version: the pastry is thicker and crunchier, the shape is more rounded, and the filling usually includes soft potato with panch phoron spices.

faqs.question: Is it vegetarian?
faqs.answer: Yes. The filling is potato, peas and spices.

faqs.question: Is it halal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every Antar product is halal certified and made without harmful preservatives.

recipes.title: Spring Rolls with Sweet Chilli Sauce
recipes.summary: Crisp rolls with a quick homemade sweet chilli dip.
ingredients: 1 tsp cornflour mixed with 1 tbsp water
steps: Simmer the sugar, vinegar, water, chilli and garlic for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cornflour mix and cook until glossy, then cool.
Fry or air-fry the spring rolls until golden.
Serve hot with the sauce.

recipes.title: Spring Roll Lettuce Wraps
recipes.summary: A fresh, crunchy way to serve spring rolls.
steps: Cook the spring rolls until crisp.
Place each roll on a lettuce leaf with herbs and cucumber.
Drizzle with sweet chilli sauce, wrap and eat.

hacks.title: Separate before cooking
hacks.body: If rolls have frozen together, tap the box gently or ease them apart with a butter knife. Don't run them under water.

hacks.title: Air-fry for less oil
hacks.body: A light spray of oil and 10–12 minutes at 180°C gives a crisp shell with much less oil than deep-frying.

faqs.question: Can I bake them?

seo.description: Shatter-crisp spring rolls filled with cabbage, carrot and onion. 10 pcs (400g), fry, air-fry or bake from frozen. Halal certified, available in Japan.

products.name: Premium Khejur Patali Gur
products.shortDescription: Winter's most precious treat — rich date-palm jaggery with deep caramel notes.
products.description:
Winter's most precious treat — rich date-palm jaggery with deep caramel notes. Enjoy it on its own, with puffed rice, or in traditional Bangladeshi sweets and payesh.

Khejur patali gur is made by slowly boiling the fresh winter sap of the date palm and setting it into round cakes. It has a smoky, caramel flavour that white sugar simply can't match.

preparation.steps: Break off a piece and enjoy it as it is, with puffed rice or after a meal.
To use in cooking, chop or grate the gur and melt it gently over low heat with a splash of water or milk.

recipes.title: Nolen Gur Payesh (Rice Pudding)
recipes.summary: Bengal's beloved winter dessert — creamy rice pudding sweetened with date-palm jaggery.
ingredients: 1/4 cup fragrant short-grain rice (kalijira or Japanese rice), washed
120g Antar Premium Khejur Patali Gur, grated
Chopped pistachios or almonds to garnish
steps: Bring the milk to a boil with the cardamom and bay leaf, then add the rice.
Simmer on low heat, stirring often, for 40–45 minutes until the rice is soft and the milk has thickened.
Turn off the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes.
Stir in the grated gur until dissolved — adding it off the heat stops the milk from curdling.
Garnish with nuts and serve warm or chilled.

recipes.title: Muri Moa (Puffed Rice & Gur Balls)
recipes.summary: Crunchy puffed rice bound with melted patali gur.
ingredients: 200g Antar Premium Khejur Patali Gur, chopped
1 tsp ghee or oil for your hands
steps: Melt the gur with the water over low heat until bubbling and slightly thick.
Remove from the heat and stir in the puffed rice quickly.
With greased hands, press into small balls while warm.
Cool completely and store airtight.

recipes.title: Gur Cha (Jaggery Milk Tea)
recipes.summary: Milk tea sweetened with patali gur for a rich, caramel flavour.
steps: Boil the water with the tea leaves and cardamom for 2 minutes.
Add the milk and bring back to a simmer.
Turn off the heat, stir in the gur until dissolved, then strain and serve.

hacks.title: Add gur off the heat
hacks.body: When sweetening milk, payesh or tea, turn off the heat and let it cool slightly before stirring in the gur. Boiling milk with jaggery can make it curdle.

hacks.title: Grate, don't chop
hacks.body: Patali gur sets firm. A box grater or the back of a knife turns it into fine shavings that melt quickly and evenly.

hacks.title: Keep it airtight
hacks.body: Gur absorbs moisture and can turn sticky. Keep it in an airtight jar, and in humid summers store it in the fridge.

faqs.question: What is khejur patali gur?
faqs.answer: It is jaggery made from the sap of the date palm tree, collected in winter and slowly boiled until it sets into round cakes. It is one of Bangladesh's most treasured seasonal foods.

faqs.question: How do I use it instead of sugar?
faqs.answer: Grate it and use it in tea, desserts, payesh, pitha or baking. It is less sweet than white sugar and adds a caramel, slightly smoky flavour.

faqs.question: Why has my gur become soft or sticky?
faqs.answer: It has absorbed moisture from the air. It is still fine to eat. Keep it in an airtight jar, and in the fridge during humid weather.

faqs.question: Is it halal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every Antar product is halal certified and made without harmful preservatives.

products.name: Plain Paratha
products.shortDescription: Soft, flaky, layered flatbread — straight from freezer to pan in minutes.
products.description:
Soft, flaky, layered flatbread — straight from freezer to pan in minutes. Perfect with curry, eggs or a cup of tea.

Each paratha is folded and layered by hand-style lamination, so it puffs into crisp, buttery-tasting layers as it cooks. No rolling, no mess — just heat and serve.

preparation.steps: Do not thaw. Heat a dry non-stick pan or tawa on medium. Cook the frozen paratha until golden spots appear, then flip and cook the other side. No oil needed.
Preheat to 180°C. Cook one paratha at a time, turning halfway, until puffed and lightly golden.

benefits: Ready in about 5 minutes, no oil needed

recipes.title: Dim Paratha (Egg Paratha)
recipes.summary: A Bangladeshi breakfast favourite — paratha cooked with spiced egg.
steps: Beat the egg with onion, chilli, coriander and salt.
Cook the paratha from frozen for about 1 minute on each side.
Pour the egg into the pan and press the paratha on top so the egg sticks to it.
Cook until the egg is set, flip and cook for 30 seconds more. Serve with tea.

recipes.title: Paratha Vegetable Roll
recipes.summary: A street-style roll filled with spiced vegetables.
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (potato, peas, carrot), cooked
1/2 tsp cumin and 1/2 tsp garam masala
steps: Sauté the vegetables with the spices and a pinch of salt for 3–4 minutes.
Cook the parathas until golden.
Spread with chutney, add the vegetables and onion, and squeeze over some lemon.
Roll up tightly and wrap the bottom in paper to serve.

hacks.title: Scrunch for extra layers
hacks.body: Right after cooking, hold the hot paratha between two spatulas (or clean, protected hands) and scrunch it gently from the sides. The layers open up and it turns extra flaky.

hacks.title: Separate while frozen
hacks.body: Peel off the film and take parathas out one at a time. Return the rest to the freezer straight away so they don't stick together.

faqs.question: Do I need to add oil or butter?
faqs.answer: No. The paratha already contains oil and cooks well in a dry pan. Add a little butter or ghee at the end if you like a richer taste.

faqs.question: Can I cook it from frozen?
faqs.answer: Yes. Always cook it straight from frozen — thawed parathas become sticky and hard to handle.

faqs.question: Is it halal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every Antar product is halal certified and made without harmful preservatives.
